supportingEvidence.title: Reuters: Qatar PM heads to Tehran as Hormuz flows remain at a three-month low
supportingEvidence.note: Reuters reports Qatar's prime minister will visit Tehran to relaunch diplomacy and cites ship-tracking data showing about 5 million b/d of Hormuz oil flow on Monday versus roughly 20 million b/d before the war.

supportingEvidence.title: Qatar Ministry of Foreign Affairs: support for temporary corridor, mine clearing and freedom of navigation
supportingEvidence.note: Primary Qatari source confirms support for Iran-Oman corridor and mine-clearing talks and explicitly calls for freedom of maritime navigation.

supportingEvidence.title: Qatar Ministry of Foreign Affairs: phased Hormuz framework remains under discussion
supportingEvidence.note: Primary Qatari source confirms ongoing Oman-Iran discussions on a phased temporary navigation route and joint demining project rather than a completed normalization state.

contradictingEvidence.title: Reuters: oil prices continue falling as markets price reopening hopes
contradictingEvidence.note: Brent and WTI continued multi-day declines, showing that market pricing is moving toward de-escalation even though observed physical flow remains deeply impaired.

contradictingEvidence.title: Reuters: Iran retains military leverage and negotiations remain unresolved
contradictingEvidence.note: The same report says Iran retains missile/drone capability, 70 maritime incidents have been recorded since the war began, and no final Iran-Oman agreement exists yet.

falsifier: Downgrade the current narrative-physical divergence if independent Hormuz oil flow rises and holds near the pre-war ~20 million b/d baseline, maritime incidents fall materially, freight/war-risk insurance normalizes, and Iran/Oman/Qatar publish compatible navigation terms that are operationally observed.

evidence.title: Reuters ship-tracking estimate and Qatar mediation report

title: Qatar mediation begins while Hormuz oil flow remains near one-quarter of pre-war baseline
summary: Qatar's prime minister is heading to Tehran to relaunch mediation and push freedom of navigation, while Reuters cites ship-tracking data showing roughly 5 million b/d through Hormuz versus about 20 million b/d before the war. Diplomatic de-escalation is advancing faster than physical normalization.
delta: Replace the recent-crisis moving average as the main normalization yardstick with the pre-war physical baseline. Treat current flows near 5 million b/d versus ~20 million b/d pre-war as severe residual impairment. Qatar's active mediation raises reopening probability but does not justify NORMALIZING until physical flow and security data confirm it.
firstOrderImpacts: continued downside pressure on crude risk premium if Qatar mediation gains traction
persistent physical supply and shipping constraints while Hormuz oil flow remains near one-quarter of pre-war levels
higher value of pre-war baseline comparisons over crisis-period moving averages
secondOrderImpacts: market prices may normalize materially ahead of physical throughput
freight, insurance and refined-product stress can remain elevated even as crude prices fall
Orbital Insight should distinguish absolute recovery from short-term momentum to avoid false normalization signals

alphaHunter.hypothesis: A pre-war absolute-flow baseline plus maritime-security telemetry will classify Hormuz normalization more accurately than crisis-period moving averages or oil-price reaction alone.
alphaHunter.baseline: diplomatic headlines, Brent/WTI reaction and recent crisis-period traffic averages
alphaHunter.alternativeData: absolute oil-flow estimates versus pre-war baseline, vessel counts, IMF PortWatch where available, maritime incident data, tanker freight, war-risk insurance and refined-product deliveries
alphaHunter.incrementalValueMetric: 3-7 day classification accuracy for SEVERE_IMPAIRMENT / CONTESTED_REOPENING / NORMALIZING using later physical-flow and logistics evidence
alphaHunter.killCondition: Kill the added baseline/security layer if it does not improve held-out normalization classification versus a simple public-headline and oil-price baseline or if the physical data arrive too late to affect decisions.
